completeness_limit: All identifiable sources for the described method found in these repository records are accounted for. Papers read outside the repository or undocumented influences cannot be inferred. Historical references are recorded, not represented as current implementation sources.

mass_momentum_revision.attribution: Mirjalili2021 motivates accounting for interface mass flux in momentum transport; Zhan2022 supports the consistent mass flux and full divergence correction. The manuscript explicitly presents the current solver as an adaptation with distinct discrete operators and conservation limitations.

section_1_6_revision.scope: Sec. 1.6 only; earlier source text including user comments preserved byte-for-byte.
section_1_6_revision.overall_motivation: Balance efficiency and stability for narrow-gap transients using local guards and thermal substeps.

formula_provenance.density_reference: Derivative of the unregularized planar tanh equilibrium profile; Hajabdollahi2021 Eqs. (2)-(3). The 1.5 factor and floor are empirical.
formula_provenance.density_scale: D2Q9 directional-product bound and a local density-weighted source budget.
formula_provenance.face_scale: Four-face acceleration budget, shared coefficients and the triangle inequality.
formula_provenance.thermal_substeps: Direct ceil-based counts from the upwind outflow-fraction and Fourier limits, 0.5 and 0.15. Advection and conduction are substepped separately; exceeding 64 aborts.
formula_provenance.refill_projection: Moment consistency under new geometry, distinguished from amplitude limiting.

thermal_intro_revision.scope: Sec. 1.6 opening and thermal substeps only, plus removal of the stale phrase "and the above repairs"; preceding sections and user-commented blocks preserved byte-for-byte.
thermal_intro_revision.opening_motivation: A large explicit thermal step can remove more water than a cell contains or cause temperature overshoots; substep thermal updates while retaining the fluid time step.
thermal_intro_revision.separate_update_intervals: Advection at every fluid step; conduction/erosion may span multiple fluid steps. Each interval is divided into its own number of equal substeps.
thermal_intro_revision.substep_cap_behavior: Abort when either count exceeds 64; do not truncate the count.
